scope.changed_factor: Only the 16 safe-slot ordering: maximum immediately prior round actual rank margin drop divided by current fixed-floor slack. Original v7 risk persistence, safe memory, weak rival coverage, 64-direction quota, 512 total direction cap, floors, solver and rank guards unchanged.

v9_final.stop_reason: All six frozen backtracking steps failed the actual safe-condition guard in round 3; no quota or floor relaxation.

comparison.note: V9 is worse even at 256 used directions; full-run endpoints also differ because v9 safely stopped early. Reused optimization TRAIN counts are not independent accuracy.

microscope.interpretation: Past update response does not reliably predict sensitivity to the next, different update. Replacing current-slack priority with that ratio displaced a currently fragile condition. This is a selection counterexample, not proof of architectural infeasibility or a human semantic boundary.

decision: Retain v7 as the research comparison champion only; reject v9 ordering. Neither candidate passes all original fixed-floor conditions, so neither is a product promotion.
next_bounded_hypothesis: Keep the current-slack-first safety prefix rather than replace it with prior response. Any further experiment must test discovery of current-trial blockers within the existing total direction budget, preserve original floors/rank guards, and independently reconstruct selection and rollback. Do not infer independent improvement from these reused TRAIN anchors.
